target_customer: Online fashion retailers and apparel brands that need on-model product images
problem: Photographing apparel on models is costly. Allure generated on-model images from a single garment photo with AI and rendering.
business_model: B2B image generation service per image
product_category: Generative AI for fashion e-commerce imagery

founders.name: Jeremy Chamoux
founders.background_notes: YC bio: generative AI, deep learning and computer vision.

founders.name: Gabrielle Chou
previous_startups: Three unnamed exits per YC bio
founders.background_notes: YC bio mentions NASDAQ-listed and Asia-Pacific experience without naming companies.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating realistic apparel on any model from one photo in 2019 needed computer vision and rendering research for an 18 person team at peak.

defensibility.rationale: Quality depended on models and data and later generative tools lowered the barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Farfetch bought 100 percent of Allure Systems Corp and its French subsidiary in December 2021, cash, price undisclosed in the sources found.

market_need_then: Photography cost per image is a retailer pain point, per coverage describing Allure's cost-per-image reduction. No 2019 spend figure found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared with many unrelated Allure companies, including a beauty tech firm and a security firm, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Allure Systems joined YC in Winter 2019 and sold to Farfetch in December 2021 to cut on-model image cost. The reported price is inconsistent across aggregators and the date varies between 1 and 20 December, so the size of the outcome is unknown. It looks like a strategic buyout rather than a failure.
notes: No company website listed in the directory. Funding unverified aggregator figures: CB Insights 3.72M over 6 rounds, PitchBook 3.85M, Employbl 3.15M, a 2017 seed led by Calao Finance and CapHorn Invest. Dealroom reports 21.7M price and Dec 1, other source Dec 20, unresolved, not entered. Competitor lists (Looklet, Veeton, StudioDrop) were current CB Insights pages with no dates near 2019, so the dated list is empty.
